newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks close slightly lower on correction.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks close slightly lower on correction.

text.p: South Korean share prices closed slightly lower on Friday in what traders said would likely be a short-term correction following two days of sharp increases.

The Korea Composite Price Index ended the day down 0.42 points to 699.53. The intraday high was 709.57. Volume and value were 50 million shares and 732 billion won. Decliners outnumbered gainers by 447 to 341.
"This correction is natural," said S.W. Choi of Schroders Securities. "I do not see stock prices plunging sharply."
Many of the core blue chip stocks that led the week's earlier rallies ended the day on Friday in negative territory.
Pohang Iron and Steel fell 700 won to 54,300, while Samsung Electronics dropped 600 won to 63,000.
However, Daewoo shares continued to rise, though at a slower pace. Traders said investors liked Daewoo shares' low prices.

After three consecutive days of going limit-up, Daewoo Heavy Industries closed up 400 won to 6,690 on Friday. Daewoo Heavy was also the most heavily traded stock of the day with more than 3.5 million shares exchanging hands.
Shares of Daewoo Corp rose by the upper daily limit to 6,640 on trading volume of 2.5 million shares.
LG Electronics rose 600 won to 12,000 with 1.4 million shares trading.
Traders said the strength of the Japanese yen continued to be the main driving force behind Korean stock prices.
But unlike earlier in the week when investors focused almost exclusively on blue chips, the interest on Friday shifted toward non-heavyweight shares.
Doosan Glass went limit-up to 9,180, as did Ke Mong Sa Publishing, which ended at 33,800 won, and Samyang Optical, which closed at 1,490.
Casey Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland said foreign investor sentiment had improved with the yen's rally against the dollar.
The yen weakened on Friday and was trading at 116.80/83 against the dollar in late afternoon in Tokyo.
"Foreigners are getting interested," Choe said. "People are pretty much aggressive for selective stocks."
Traders said the index would rise gradually, but would face strong resistance at about 720.
"There are still a lot of shares waiting for a selling spree at 720," Choe said.
